source.author: ov
source.text: Hunc pede convulso mensae Pellaeus acernae stravit humi Pelates deiecto in pectora mento, cumque atro mixtos sputantem sanguine dentes vulnere Tartareas geminato mittit ad umbras.
source.text_original: Hunc pede convulso mensae Pellaeus acernae / stravit humi Pelates deiecto in pectora mento, / cumque atro mixtos sputantem sanguine dentes / vulnere Tartareas geminato mittit ad umbras.
source.text_english: With his foot wrenched free, the man from Pella hurled Pelates, the son of the oak, down onto the ground from the maple table, with his chin forced down upon his breast; and when he was spitting out his teeth, mixed with black blood, from the doubled wound, he sent him to the Tartarean shades.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: crateres mensaeque volant araeque deorum poculaque, insignis veterum labor.
reuse.text_original: crateres mensaeque volant araeque deorum / poculaque, insignis veterum labor.
reuse.text_english: craters and tables and altars of the gods fly about, and cups, a notable workmanship of the ancients.
